planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized transplants in late winter through early spring; space 3-4 feet apart. Chattooga is a University of Arkansas erect thornless blackberry noted for ripening earlier in the season than most other thornless cultivars.

directions: Plant dormant canes in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil (pH 6.0-6.5) in full sun; Chattooga is a University of Arkansas erect thornless blackberry release valued for ripening earlier in the season than most other thornless cultivars, extending the harvest window at the front end. It produces medium to large, firm, glossy black berries with good flavor on vigorous, upright canes that need only modest trellising support. Its early ripening makes it a useful companion to later-season thornless cultivars for a longer overall blackberry harvest. Prune out fruited floricanes immediately after harvest and thin new primocanes to the sturdiest few per plant to maintain good air circulation and fruit size.
